title: Gradient Descent & Optimizers — Walk Downhill in Fog
key_insight: A gradient tells how loss changes around the current weights. Gradient descent moves weights in the opposite direction because that direction lowers loss nearby.
body:
## Walk Downhill in Fog

A hiker cannot see the whole valley but can feel which direction slopes downward. One careful step should move closer to the low point.

A gradient tells how loss changes around the current weights. Gradient descent moves weights in the opposite direction because that direction lowers loss nearby.

Training repeats: predict, measure loss, find gradients, and update. One step rarely solves the whole problem.
common_mistakes: An optimizer creates training labels from nothing.
Weights should move in the direction that raises loss.
Momentum deletes all information from earlier steps.
mini_exercise: Sketch the situation in “Walk Downhill in Fog” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Backpropagation finds directions; the optimizer decides the actual size and pattern of every update.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Walk Downhill in Fog” situation, explain Gradient Descent & Optimizers without assuming the listener knows deep learning.
